summary: Calimesa sits in the San Gorgonio Pass, that dramatic wind-carved corridor between the San Bernardino Mountains and the San Jacinto range, which means you can stand in a parking lot and see 10,000-foot peaks in two directions — a setting that makes the city's modest 11,000 population and 14.9 square miles feel far more cinematic than its census data would suggest. At a median home price of $423,300 against a median household income of $90,313, the price-to-income ratio lands around 4.7 — notably more accessible than most of the Inland Empire's westward neighbors, though the tradeoff is geographic isolation from major job centers like Riverside or Ontario, making this firmly a bedroom community where the commute via I-10 is the daily tax. The pass funnels reliable afternoon wind, which pairs with 9.8 hours of daily sunshine and a 75°F average high to create a climate that runs hot and dry in summer but stays remarkably mild through winter — genuine four-season outdoor weather without a real winter. Retail and dining options are sparse and highway-commercial in character; serious grocery variety or restaurant depth means driving toward Redlands or Beaumont. Violent crime is low at 90 per 100K, though property crime — especially larceny at 1,597 per 100K — runs high enough to notice. Calimesa is essentially a mountain-framed affordability play whose defining equation is cheaper housing traded against longer drives and thinner local amenities.
